quick.topic: Map the journey, mark the low point
quick.summary: How a journey map shows where to design first.
quick.takeaway: Stages, actions, feelings. Design for the lowest point first.

parts.title: Map the journey, mark the low point

beats.line: I have notes from ten interviews about booking a repair. How do I show the team?
Draw a journey map. Four steps.
First, the stages, from noticing the problem to the repair done.
Second, what the person does at each stage.
Third, how they feel there. Use their own words.
Fourth, mark the lowest point. That is where design helps most.
Isn’t it just a pretty poster?
Only if nothing follows. Tie the low point to a design decision.
Lowest point: waiting with no news. So we design status updates first.
Now the map earned its wall space.

quiz.question: What makes a journey map useful to a product team?
options: It ties the lowest point to a design decision
It covers every stage in the same detail
It is polished enough to hang on the wall
It describes the product’s screens in order
quiz.explanation: A map helps when it shows where people struggle most and leads to a decision about what to design.

quiz.question: A journey map should record how people feel at each stage, not only what they do.
quiz.explanation: Feelings show where the experience breaks down, which is where design effort pays off most.
